hero.lead: The largest landlocked nation on earth, home to 20.8 million, where oil, gas and minerals earn a quarter of the economy and a World Bank guarantee of $846 million in February 2026 mobilises $1.41 billion of private finance for rail.

capital.heading: Guarantees that bring private capital to the steppe.

record.text: IBRD guarantee for rail connectivity and logistics, mobilising $1.41 billion of private financing, February 2026

General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Sovereign Eurobonds, June 2025
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · issued 24 June 2025 · 7-year tranche US$1.35bn, coupon 5% · 12-year tranche US$1.15bn, coupon 5.5% · demand more than twice the offer
register.note: Listed on the London Stock Exchange, the AIFC Exchange and the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange
register.text: Sovereign US dollar Eurobonds of the Republic of Kazakhstan in two tranches, at yields the Ministry of Finance describes as comparable to those of sovereign issuers with higher credit ratings (A/AA). With them the Ministry completed the full refinancing of its Eurobonds maturing in 2025, which bears on the public finances that pay for public services.

register.name: Advancing Learning, Entrepreneurship and Markets for Artificial Intelligence (ALEM)
register.detail: IBRD loan of JPY 11,999.7 million · approved 30 September 2026 · P513072 · Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development, with Astana Hub and Alem Capital Management
register.note: Aims at 10,000 jobs and at least $60 million of private capital by December 2031
register.text: An IBRD loan to enable the creation, commercialisation and scale-up of technology start-ups in Kazakhstan. It aims at the creation of 10,000 jobs and at mobilising at least $60 million in private capital by December 2031, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: MIGA guarantees for the national road maintenance loan
register.detail: MIGA guarantees to Standard Chartered, J.P. Morgan and Commerzbank · loan of $785 million to the Development Bank of Kazakhstan, on-lent to KazAvtoZhol · 13 July 2026 · part of a $2 billion programme with an EIB loan of €200 million
register.note: Construction will support an estimated 25,000 jobs a year
register.text: MIGA guarantees cover a commercial loan of $785 million to the Development Bank of Kazakhstan, which on-lends it to the national road operator for regular maintenance and medium repairs of around 7,700 kilometres of roads, including sections of the North–South and Trans-Caspian corridors. MIGA estimates that construction will support 25,000 jobs a year, which bears on the livelihood standard.

register.name: Policy reforms for jobs and inclusive growth
register.detail: IBRD loan · Second Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth Development Policy Operation · approved 13 March 2026 · AIIB co-financing of $400 million approved 23 April 2026
register.text: Budget support for Kazakhstan’s reform agenda, to create more and better-paid jobs with the private sector as the main job creator. The reforms cover energy pricing and efficiency, renewables, digital connectivity, wider access to social assistance and water conservation, which bear on the energy, water and livelihood standards.
register.note: Supports energy pricing and efficiency, renewables, social assistance and water conservation

register.name: Rail connectivity and logistics guarantee
register.detail: IBRD guarantee · approved 19 February 2026 · Transforming Rail Connectivity in Kazakhstan (Middle Corridor Development), P512386 · AIIB co-guarantee of $564 million
register.text: An IBRD guarantee, with a co-guarantee from the AIIB, that mobilises $1.41 billion of private financing for rail. It finances a new 322.3-kilometre railway line between Mointy and Kyzylzhar, which shortens the corridor by 149 kilometres; the World Bank expects it to stimulate job creation in communities along the new line, which bears on the livelihood standard.
register.note: Mobilises $1.41 billion of long-term commercial financing

register.name: Transport Resilience and Connectivity: Jezkazgan to Karagandy (Middle Corridor)
register.detail: IBRD loan of JPY 94.4 billion · approved 15 November 2024 · P500565 · KazAvtoZhol, with a sovereign guarantee · closing 30 June 2032 · AIIB co-financing of $650 million
register.text: An IBRD loan, with AIIB co-financing under a separate agreement, to upgrade the Jezkazgan–Karagandy section of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route into a climate-resilient dual carriageway, with rural last-mile roads. The project offers jobs and internships in the road sector to support women’s economic participation, which bears on the livelihood standard.
register.note: Total project cost $1.53 billion for a 498 km dual carriageway (AIIB)

register.name: Almaty power grid modernisation, Alatau Zharyk Company
register.detail: EBRD long-term loan of up to KZT 102 billion (€194 million equivalent) · September 2026 · borrower a fully owned subsidiary of Samruk Energy
register.note: Automated metering, telemechanics, smart meters at substations and pilot smart grid technologies
register.text: A long-term EBRD loan in tenge to Alatau Zharyk Company, a fully owned subsidiary of Samruk Energy, for the power grid of Almaty and the Almaty region. It finances automated metering and telemechanic equipment, upgraded low- and medium-voltage networks, pilot smart grid technologies and cybersecurity, which bears on the energy standard.

register.name: Development of Economic and Industrial Zones Project
register.detail: Islamic Development Bank · KAZ1038 · approved 2026 · guarantee agreement exchanged in Astana on 1 July 2026 with the Industrial Development Fund
register.note: IsDB approvals for Kazakhstan since 1996 totalled US$1.64 billion by June 2024
register.text: Financing of the Islamic Development Bank to strengthen Kazakhstan’s economic and industrial zones, with a guarantee agreement signed by the Industrial Development Fund. It supports the nation’s efforts to attract investment, create jobs and advance long-term economic diversification, which bears on the livelihood standard.

register.name: Fiscal Governance and Financial Sector Reforms Program, subprogram 2
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · policy-based loan, $500 million equivalent · approved 11 June 2026
register.note: A 15-year ADB loan agreement of 3.4 billion yuan for priority budget expenditures, signed 11 September 2026, was ratified by law (Trend, 4 November 2026)
register.text: An ADB policy-based loan for more robust fiscal rules, better management of fiscal savings and of the National Fund, a single legal framework for public–private partnerships and stronger financial regulation and supervision. It also integrates gender and climate considerations into budgeting, and it serves the public finances.

register.name: Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth Development Policy Operation: AIIB co-financing
register.detail: AIIB · P000999 · approved 23 April 2026 · borrower the Minister of Finance · World Bank lead financier
register.note: Co-financing with the World Bank, the lead financier, in the energy sector
register.text: AIIB co-financing of the World Bank’s development policy operation, to help the Government of Kazakhstan implement crucial policy reforms and support the transition to a greener economy. The reforms cover energy pricing and efficiency, renewables and social assistance, which bear on the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Affordable housing finance for women and green mortgages, Otbasy Bank
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · loan of 90 billion tenge ($173.6 million equivalent) · approved 1 April 2026 · with a $500,000 technical assistance grant financed equally with Otbasy Bank
register.note: Mortgages for more than 2,000 eligible households, prioritising women borrowers
register.text: An ADB loan in tenge to Otbasy Bank to expand access to affordable housing finance for women and to offer green mortgage products to low- and moderate-income households across Kazakhstan. It will finance mortgages for more than 2,000 households and support a green mortgage framework that other banks can replicate, which serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Framework loan to the Development Bank of Kazakhstan for energy and transport
register.detail: EIB Global · signed 23 December 2024 · announced 13 March 2025 · backed by guarantees from the European Commission
register.note: MIGA names a €200 million EIB loan in the same $2 billion road programme (13 July 2026)
register.text: A strategic framework loan of EIB Global to the Development Bank of Kazakhstan, which funds investments by public and private entities. It finances renewable electricity generation to help Kazakhstan shift away from fossil fuels and the national road operator’s programme to rehabilitate 5,000 km of national and regional roads, which bears on the energy standard.

register.name: EBRD loans to KMF Bank
register.detail: EBRD · up to US$50 million (€43.4 million) · 2026 · with the Advice for Small Businesses programme · supported by the government of Kazakhstan
register.note: In 2025 the EBRD lent KMF up to US$25 million for women entrepreneurs
register.text: An EBRD financing package of up to US$50 million for KMF Bank, an EBRD client since 2005, complemented by advisory services, training, networking and mentoring. KMF lends to micro and small businesses, and over 55 percent of its borrowers are women and 67 percent live in rural areas (IFC, 2024), which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Local currency loan to Arnur Credit for micro and small businesses
register.detail: IFC · $10 million-equivalent · signed 14 July 2025 · $5 million from IFC and $5 million mobilised from Invest in Visions · Canada-IFC GROW Facility
register.note: Forty percent earmarked for women-run businesses; the EBRD also lent Arnur Credit up to US$7 million in 2025 under Youth in Business
register.text: A local currency loan from IFC’s MSME Finance Platform to Arnur Credit, a microfinance institution that serves more than 25,000 clients in rural areas of Southern Kazakhstan. It expands financing for micro and small enterprises, 40 percent of it for women-run businesses, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: CPIH Kazakhstan 220 MW wind portfolio
register.detail: AIIB nonsovereign financing · P000823 · approved 16 January 2025 · five wind power plants in Akmola Region · China Power International Holding
register.note: With a 42 km 220 kV double-circuit line and the expansion of a 220 kV substation
register.text: AIIB financing for five wind power plants with 220 MW of turbines in the Akmola Region, developed and operated by companies of China Power International Holding, a subsidiary of State Power Investment Corporation. It adds renewable electricity to Kazakhstan’s grid, which bears on the energy standard.

register.name: IFC investment in KMF for micro and small businesses
register.detail: IFC · up to $50 million · Almaty, 10 September 2024 · supports KMF’s transformation into a bank with a strong focus on micro and small enterprises
register.note: IFC had earlier provided KMF with financial products totalling $287 million
register.text: An IFC investment of up to $50 million in KMF, one of the country’s leading microfinance institutions, with 18 branches and 117 sales points, to boost financing for micro and small enterprises, with a focus on women entrepreneurs and rural agribusinesses. Over 55 percent of its borrowers are women and 67 percent live in rural areas, which bears on the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Oil and Gas
items.label: Of GDP from oil and gas rents, 2021
items.text: Caspian oil and gas: rents worth a sixth of the economy.

items.name: The Minerals
items.label: Of GDP from mineral rents, 2021
items.text: Copper, uranium and other metals: mineral rents worth 9% of the economy.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: The steppe: grain and grazing across four fifths of the land.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: The largest landlocked territory on earth, on the overland route from China to Europe.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 29.1% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Global Kishkentai
items.text: A maker of wooden educational toys that began with toys for preschool children with disabilities and now also makes programming kits, with the start-up CodiPlay, for schoolchildren in Kazakhstan, South Korea and Saudi Arabia, with an average monthly turnover of ₸12 million.

items.name: AR Sana
items.text: An Almaty start-up whose mobile app uses artificial intelligence and augmented-reality games to help Kazakh-speaking children from about 18 months develop their speech, with a web platform for speech therapists; more than 35 specialists use it in five centres and two schools, and parents pay $9.99 a month for full access.

items.name: KMF Bank
items.text: One of the country’s leading lenders to micro and small businesses, now a bank, with 18 branches and 117 sales points; over 55 percent of its borrowers are women and 67 percent live in rural areas.

items.name: Arnur Credit
items.text: A microfinance institution that serves more than 25,000 clients in rural areas of Southern Kazakhstan, with about half of its loan portfolio dedicated to women-led businesses.

items.name: Kunde café
items.text: A social café, begun as a student volunteer project, that employs people with disabilities: about 50 staff, including 25 people with special needs in Astana and 12 in Almaty, at one café in Astana and two in Almaty, among them a coffee island in Atakent Mall built for wheelchair users.

items.name: GreenTal
items.text: A company of carpentry and sewing workshops and a printing shop that employs people from socially vulnerable groups, among them single mothers and people who have served prison sentences; its founders also run a coffee shop, showroom and Social Innovation Hub for the products of 11 inclusive workshops.
